title: Advanced Patterns & Routing
subtitle: Context, Custom Hooks, Performance & Navigation - Senior Dev Level
description: Master Context API to avoid prop drilling, custom hooks to reuse logic, memo for performance, and React Router for navigation - exactly how your dashboard navigates between lessons.

blocks.text: PAGE 1: The Problem - Prop Drilling Hell in Your Dashboard

Hey! In Lesson 3 you learned prop drilling: App -> Navbar -> Header -> UserAvatar passing user name through 3 levels even though Navbar and Header don't need it. In your dashboard you have XP, coins, user, theme, lessons - if you drill through 5 levels, nightmare! Every middle component receives props just to pass down. Hard to maintain.

Solution 1: Context API - Create global store: XP, user, theme available anywhere without drilling. Solution 2: Custom Hooks - Extract reusable logic like useLocalStorage, useFetch, useXP. Solution 3: React Router - Navigate between /react, /lesson/1, /profile without page reload. Solution 4: Performance - memo, useMemo, useCallback to avoid unnecessary re-renders when you have 10 lesson cards.
Today you become senior dev - these 4 patterns separate junior (props drilling everywhere) from senior (clean architecture). Your Lesson 10 final app NEEDS these.

blocks.question: APPLICATION: Your dashboard has 5 levels: App -> CoursePage -> LessonGrid -> LessonCard -> CompleteButton. CompleteButton needs addXP function from App. Without Context, how many levels of prop drilling?
options: 4 levels - App passes to CoursePage, to LessonGrid, to LessonCard, to CompleteButton - all middle components receive addXP just to pass down, even if they don't use it
Prop drilling is not needed in React
blocks.correctFeedback: Yes! 4 levels of drilling - messy! Context solves this - CompleteButton uses useContext directly, middle components don't need to know about XP.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Prop drilling: Each level passes prop down. 5 levels = 4 drilling steps. Context = 0 drilling, direct access anywhere.
blocks.reasoning: Context API eliminates prop drilling for global data like XP, user, theme.

blocks.text: PAGE 3: Custom Hooks - Reuse Logic Like useLocalStorage, useFetch

You wrote useEffect for localStorage save in Lesson 5, and fetch logic in Lesson 5 example 8. If you need same logic in 5 components, you copy paste useEffect 5 times - duplication! Custom Hook extracts logic into reusable function: useLocalStorage(key, initialValue) that any component can use. Rule: Custom hook name must start with use, and can call other hooks inside.

blocks.title: Example 2: Custom Hooks - useLocalStorage and useFetch (Your Dashboard Needs Both)
blocks.output:

blocks.question: APPLICATION: You need localStorage for XP in Navbar, LessonCard, and ProfilePage - 3 components. Without custom hook, what happens?
options: Write same useState + useEffect localStorage logic 3 times - duplication, hard to maintain
Create custom hook useLocalStorage once, use in 3 components: const [xp, setXp] = useLocalStorage('xp', 0) - DRY, maintainable
Only one component can use localStorage
blocks.correctFeedback: Exactly! Custom hook = Write once, use everywhere. That's senior dev DRY principle - Don't Repeat Yourself.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Custom hooks extract reusable logic. useLocalStorage encapsulates get + set + useEffect save. Use in any component with one line.
blocks.reasoning: Custom hooks are essential for reusable logic across components.

blocks.text: PAGE 4: React Router - Navigation Without Page Reload (Your Dashboard Navigation)

Your dashboard has: / (home), /react (React course page you gave me), /lesson/1, /lesson/2, /profile. In old HTML, each navigation reloads page. In React SPA with React Router, navigation is instant - no reload, state preserved, XP stays, just component changes. That's why your backBtn and Start Lesson buttons should use Router, not window.location.

blocks.question: APPLICATION: In your dashboard, user is on /react page with 150 XP. Clicks Start Lesson 2. You want to go to /lesson/2 without losing XP state and without page reload. How?
options: Use window.location = '/lesson/2' - causes full page reload, state lost, XP resets to 0, slow
Use React Router Link or useNavigate('/lesson/2') - SPA navigation, no reload, state preserved, instant, XP stays 150
You must reload page for navigation
blocks.correctFeedback: Yes! React Router = SPA navigation, no reload, state stays. window.location = MPA, reload, state lost. That's why your app needs Router for Lesson 10!
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Router: <Link to='/lesson/2'> or navigate('/lesson/2') - no reload, state preserved. window.location = reload, state lost.
blocks.reasoning: SPA routing preserves state and is instant - essential for dashboard navigation.

blocks.text: PAGE 5: Performance - memo, useMemo, useCallback (Your 10 Cards Re-render Problem)

You have 10 LessonCards. When XP changes in Navbar, App re-renders, all 10 LessonCards re-render too even though their props didn't change - wasted work! For 10 cards it's okay, for 1000 it's slow. Solution: React.memo - memoizes component, only re-renders if props actually changed. useMemo - memoizes expensive calculation. useCallback - memoizes function to avoid recreating each render.

blocks.title: Example 4: Performance - memo Prevents Unnecessary Re-renders
blocks.output:
XP: 0 Completed: 0 [+10 XP]
Rendering Intro (normal - waste)
Memo rendering Intro only once (optimized)

blocks.question: APPLICATION: Your dashboard has 50 lesson cards. User types in search input (search state changes). Without memo, what happens?
options: All 50 lesson cards re-render even though their props didn't change (only search changed) - wasteful, slow for 50 cards
blocks.correctFeedback: Yes! Parent state change re-renders all children by default. memo prevents re-render if props same - crucial for large lists!
blocks.incorrectFeedback: By default, parent re-render = all children re-render. memo checks props, if same, skip re-render. Saves performance for 50 cards.
blocks.reasoning: Performance optimization with memo is essential for large lists like your dashboard.

blocks.text: PAGE 7: Error Boundaries and Suspense - What Happens When Component Crashes?

What if LessonCard crashes due to bug? Without error boundary, entire app crashes - white screen! Error Boundary catches error and shows fallback UI: 'Something went wrong - Retry'. Suspense handles loading states for code splitting and data fetching - shows fallback spinner while component loads. Your dashboard has loading spinner and error states - now you know advanced version.

blocks.text: PAGE 8: Code Splitting - Load Only What You Need (Your App Is Getting Big!)

Your final Lesson 10 app will have 10 lessons, dashboard, profile, settings - big bundle! If user opens home page, why load all 10 lessons code? Code splitting with React.lazy and Suspense loads component only when needed: const LessonPage = lazy(() => import('./LessonPage')) - code for LessonPage only downloaded when user navigates to /lesson/:id. Makes initial load fast - crucial for mobile users in Ghana!

blocks.title: Example 7: Code Splitting - Fast Initial Load
blocks.output:
First load: Home page fast (small bundle)
Click Lesson -> Loading spinner 0.5s -> Lesson page appears (chunk loaded)

blocks.question: APPLICATION: Your Code Academy app final bundle is 800kb with all 10 lessons. Users on slow 3G in Accra wait 8 seconds initial load. How to make initial load 2 seconds?
options: Use React.lazy + Suspense code splitting - split each lesson page into separate chunk, initial load only home + course list (150kb), lesson chunks load on demand when user clicks Start Lesson
blocks.correctFeedback: Yes! Code splitting = fast initial load + on-demand chunks. Essential for mobile users with slow network!
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Lazy load: const LessonPage = lazy(()=>import('./LessonPage')) + <Suspense fallback={spinner}>. Initial bundle small, chunks load when needed.
blocks.reasoning: Code splitting optimizes loading performance for large apps.

blocks.text: PAGE 10: Summary - You Are Now Senior Dev Ready for Final App

You mastered today: Context API - createContext + Provider value + useContext anywhere to avoid prop drilling for XP/user/theme, Custom Hooks - useLocalStorage, useFetch - extract reusable logic, start name with use, can call other hooks, React Router - BrowserRouter + Routes + Route + Link + useParams + useNavigate for SPA navigation without reload, Performance - memo(Component) prevents re-render if props same, useMemo for expensive calculations, useCallback for stable functions, Compound Components - <Card><Card.Header><Card.Title> flexible composition via Context, Error Boundaries - class component catches crash, shows fallback, not white screen, Code Splitting - lazy(()=>import()) + Suspense fallback for on-demand chunks, fast initial load.

blocks.question: MASTER APPLICATION: Your final Lesson 10 app needs: XP accessible in Navbar, LessonCards, Profile without drilling, reusable fetch logic, navigation /react to /lesson/:id without reload, 50 lesson cards not re-rendering on every XP change, and fast initial load on 3G. Which stack?
options: Props drilling for XP, copy-paste fetch logic, window.location for navigation, no memo, one big bundle

Context for XP global store, custom hook useFetch for reusable fetch, React Router Link/navigate for SPA navigation, memo + useMemo + useCallback for 50 cards performance, lazy + Suspense code splitting for fast initial load - senior architecture
blocks.correctFeedback: PERFECT! You just designed senior-level architecture - Context + Custom Hooks + Router + Performance + Code Splitting. This is exactly what Lesson 10 complete app needs. You are job-ready!
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Senior stack: Context eliminates drilling, Custom Hooks DRY, Router SPA navigation, memo/useMemo/useCallback performance, lazy/Suspense fast load. Combined = production app.
blocks.reasoning: Combining all advanced patterns builds scalable production apps like your Code Academy dashboard.

blocks.question: When to use Context vs Props?
options: Use props for direct parent-child (1-2 levels), Context for global data needed in many places at different nesting levels (XP, user, theme, auth) to avoid drilling through 4+ levels
blocks.correctFeedback: Yes! Props for direct, Context for global. Don't overuse Context - only for truly global data, otherwise props is simpler!
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Props = explicit, good for 1-2 levels. Context = global, good for XP/user/theme needed everywhere. Use right tool for right depth.
blocks.reasoning: Knowing when to use Context vs Props is key architectural decision.
